doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Early trumpet favorites and later playing with Lunceford alumni
summary: Harry James as the first favorite heard on radio; later playing with Snooky Young, Gerald Wilson, Trummy Young and Jimmy Crawford.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Who were some of the trumpet players that you favored at that time?

The first trumpet that I favored was Harry James because he was the one that you could hear on the radio all the time. We didn’t hear Louis Armstrong on the radio, not in Phoenix. But Harry James was the most popular trumpet player in the United States, and Miles said he favored Harry James too because that’s what we heard. Then later on, you hear other people, like Roy Eldridge came to town. But Harry James was a good player, and I’m not gonna put him down ‘cause he was white.
Do you remember anybody that was in the Lunceford trumpet section or in that band?

Yeah, I played with some of the guys later, Snooky Young, lead trumpet player. Gerald Wilson, I played with his band out in California. Trummy Young, trombone player, I played with him on the jazz festival in New York. James Crawford, the drummer, I played with him in the pit band here in New York City years ago. That’s like playing with your idols.
